sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The ⏱ millisecond toggle was missing entirely from the "Length" header on single-table pageTypes (`place-performances-filtered`, `work-recordings-filtered`, `artist-relationships-filtered`, and every other `tableMode: 'single'` page). Those pages build their header layout AFTER `renderFinalTable()` returns — `startFetchingProcess()` only calls `makeTableSortableUnified()`, which creates the `.mb-col-hdr-flex` the button is inserted into, several steps later — so the render tail's own injection found no flex row and silently did nothing. The button then appeared only if some unrelated later re-render happened to run that tail again, which is why the same page could have it or not depending on whether anything had been filtered or sorted yet: reported live on `place-performances-filtered`, where the 398-row "Recording location for recording" sub-table had no button at all while the 1-row "Shooting location for recording" one did. Now also injected right after `makeTableSortableUnified()`/`initCollapsableColumns()` in the single-table path; the injection is idempotent, so the two call sites never fight. The multi-table path was never affected — `renderGroupedTable()` calls `makeTableSortableUnified()` inside its own group loop, well before its tail.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Expanded the "mb. SUPER MIND CONTROL Ⅱ X TURBO" third-party attribution block: it now credits `RECORDING_LENGTH_COLUMN` alongside `RELEASE_EVENT_COLUMN`, records that the ⏱ millisecond track-length feature and the "Release events" column are both INSPIRED BY and modelled on jesus2099's code — not copied from it, and not dependent on it at runtime — and names the two ideas taken directly from his implementation (the single per-page-entity Web Service call rather than one request per row, and the `[H:]M:SS.mmm` display shape his `time()` helper produces, which `_msFormatDuration()` reproduces so both scripts read consistently where both are installed). Also notes that jesus2099 in turn credits loujine's `mbz-showperformancedurations.user.js` as the inspiration for `RECORDING_LENGTH_COLUMN`, and refreshes the recorded `@version` from 2026.1.9 to 2026.5.21.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Millisecond track lengths now also work on the six pageTypes that have no sub-second data in the page itself — `work-recordings`, `artist-relationships`, `place-performances` and their `-filtered` twins (verified: `"length"` does not appear in a single one of a work page's embedded JSON blobs). They are fed by one MusicBrainz Web Service call, `/ws/2/{work|artist|place}/{mbid}?inc=recording-rels`, which returns every recording relationship of the page entity with its length — one request for the whole table, not one per row.

That request is made ONLY when the ⏱ toggle is first pressed, never while the page renders, so a page you don't ask for precision on costs nothing. The glyph shows ⏳ while it is in flight, and the response is cached for as long as you stay on the page: sorting, filtering and switching the toggle off and on again all work from that single response. A failure is cached too and dims the toggle with an explanation, rather than retrying on every click or quietly doing nothing. The tooltip says in advance whether a press will fetch, since on a release page it never does.

Declared per pageType via the new `features.msTrackLengthWs2`, so the toggle is only offered where a source actually exists — a page with neither an embedded payload nor that declaration gets no button rather than a dead one.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Same discard rule as the embedded source, and it earns its keep here: a Web Service value whose rounded seconds disagree with what MusicBrainz already displays is thrown away rather than rendered, since that can only mean the row was matched to the wrong recording. MusicBrainz does populate this column natively on these pages and it rounds there too (5:34.866 is displayed as "5:35"), so the check is meaningful — and it doubles as a guard against a mis-resolved column index, which would then stamp nothing instead of writing durations into some other column. Rows MusicBrainz shows as "?:??" have no length on record and stay unknown in both modes.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Millisecond track lengths on release pages. MusicBrainz stores every track length in milliseconds but only ever displays it rounded to the nearest second — a new ⏱ toggle at the left edge of the "Length" column header re-renders the whole column at full precision ("4:50" → "4:50.160") and back. It costs no network request at all: the values are already embedded in the page MusicBrainz served, in the tracklist component's own `<script type="application/json">` payload. The toggle is page-wide, so on a multi-medium release every medium switches together instead of leaving one disc reading seconds and another milliseconds. Gated by "Enable millisecond track lengths" (default: ON, new ⏱️ TRACK LENGTH PRECISION section); with it off no toggle is injected, nothing is stamped, and the column renders exactly as before.

Sorting, filtering, highlighting and the 📊 unique-values dropdown all follow whatever precision the column is currently showing, with no per-consumer work — they already read the column's rendered text. So you can filter for ".666", and "Length info - Deviation" simply becomes finer-grained. Toggling rewrites the captured source rows and re-renders through `runFilter()`, which is what keeps the active filters, their highlighting and the current sort order intact.

New "Hide a '.000' millisecond part" setting (default: OFF). MusicBrainz stores a length entered as plain "m:ss" with zero milliseconds, so ".000" means "no sub-second data on record" rather than "exactly zero"; switching this on renders those as plain "3:19". Off by default because uniform width keeps the column easier to scan.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: The value revealed is the TRACK length (`tracks[].length`), never the underlying RECORDING's length — two different MusicBrainz fields that differ constantly: on `Born to Run` four of eight tracks disagree, one by three whole seconds. MusicBrainz renders the track length, ROUNDED, which is provable from that same release (`Tenth Avenue Freeze‐Out` displays "3:12", a value only 3:11.666 rounds to and never 3:11.000). The feature's contract is therefore "reveal more precision in the number already on screen", never "show a different measurement", and it is enforced at runtime: a stamped value whose rounded seconds disagree with what MusicBrainz rendered is discarded rather than displayed. Toggling back restores the original string verbatim rather than recomputing it, since recomputing could not reproduce MusicBrainz's rounding.

Resynced `ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt` (new "TRACK LENGTH PRECISION" section, the ⏱️ settings block, and a note on the new duration-aware Length sorting under "NUMERIC COLUMN ALIGNMENT") and `CLAUDE.md` (new "Track length precision and the `treleases` trap" section, plus the new `length` debug channel).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Stop deleting MusicBrainz's own `treleases` class from release tracklists. `treleases` is genuine MusicBrainz markup there — a release page natively renders its Length column as `<th class="treleases">` plus one `<td class="treleases">` per track (verified in `tests/snapshots/release-tracks/raw.html`, which the Playwright harness captures with only this script loaded: 9 occurrences, and not one `jesus2099` string, plugin `title` or yellow `text-shadow` in the whole file). jesus2099's `RECORDING_LENGTH_COLUMN` merely reuses the same class name on the page types MusicBrainz does NOT mark (work, artist-relationships, place-performances), and never adds it alone — the same statements also set its own script name as the `title` and, on the header, a yellow `text-shadow`. New `_isJesus2099Treleases()` tests for exactly that co-occurrence, so a bare `treleases` is now recognised as MusicBrainz's and left alone.

Three places keyed on the bare class and are now gated on that predicate: the WIP.1 artifact purge (which had started stripping it from the Length `<th>`), `applyColumnErasers()`'s `'jesus2099-any'` Strategy 3b (which had been emptying `class`/`style`/`title` on all eight Length `<td>`s of every release tracklist — a pre-existing defect, visible in the committed `release-tracks` snapshot baseline as `<td class="">`), and `initTreleasesObserver()`'s dispatch (which fired `_repairTreleasesTd()` on our own freshly-rendered native cells, rebuilding them from plain `textContent` and so discarding any filter-highlight spans inside them). The predicate is conservative by construction: with no corroborating evidence the class is left in place, so the failure direction is "a stale third-party class survives", never "native markup is deleted".

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Sorting a "Length" column no longer treats MusicBrainz's own "?:??" unknown-duration placeholder as a zero-length recording. It was compared with `parseFloat(text.replace(/[^0-9.-]/g, '')) || 0`, which collapsed "?:??" to 0 and so floated every unknown-length row to the TOP of an ascending sort (descending already put them last, by the same accident). Unknown length is absent data, not zero length, so those rows are now pinned LAST in both directions — in single-column sorts and as a tie-breaker inside a Ctrl+Click multi-column chain alike.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: New explicit duration comparator for "Length" columns: `_parseDurationToMs()` parses `M:SS`, `M:SS.mmm` and `H:MM:SS[.mmm]` (right-padding a short fractional part, so ".5" is 500 ms), and `_compareDurations()` orders on real milliseconds. The previous digits-only `parseFloat` path happened to order genuine durations correctly — seconds are always zero-padded, so "5:05.146" became 505.146 and stayed monotonic — but only by relying on that undocumented invariant.

`createSortComparator()` and `createMultiColumnComparator()` now resolve a column's comparison kind through one shared `_sortColumnKind()` (`'duration'`/`'numeric'`/`'text'`) instead of disagreeing: the single-column path consulted the page definition's own `integerColumns` descriptors and only then a name heuristic, while the multi-column path used the raw header text alone and never looked at the page definition at all. `createSortComparator()`'s third argument changes from an `isNumeric` boolean to that kind string. Duration detection is data-driven — `integerColumns`' `align: ':'` descriptor already means "colon-split duration" — plus an exact `"Length"` name match, so a pageType that renders durations without declaring an `integerColumns` entry for them (`release-discids`' per-disc totals) sorts as a duration too. Alt+Click "sort by column length" still outranks the column's kind, durations included.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The final rendered table no longer carries any leftovers from jesus2099's userscripts. The reported case was the "Length" column header arriving as `<th class="treleases mb-original-column" title="SUPER MIND CONTROL Ⅱ X TURBO" style="text-shadow: yellow 0px 0px 2px; …">` — jesus2099's "mb. SUPER MIND CONTROL Ⅱ X TURBO" mutates the native header and cells in place before this script scrapes them, and `makeTableSortableUnified()` rebuilds `th.innerHTML` without ever resetting `className`/`title`/`style`, so all three rode straight through into our own header. Same for every Length `<td>` and, on release pages, for the whole `jesus2099userjs81127*` tracklist family (`toolzone`/`editbutt`/`openEdits` hover buttons, plus markers stamped onto the recording title link and Title cell). New `purgeJesus2099Artifacts()`/`_stripJesus2099InTable()` now clean every rendered `table.tbl` — header row included — on both render paths.

The purge also runs over the captured source rows in `groupedRows`/`allRows`, not just the live DOM. `runFilter()` re-renders by inserting `cloneNode(true)` copies of those rows and classes/attributes survive cloning, so cleaning only the live table would have pasted every marker back in on the next filter keystroke.

Three dispositions, so nothing real is ever destroyed: jesus2099's cover-art icon family is skipped entirely (it already has its own deliberately gated handling in `applyColumnErasers()`'s Strategy 2 and `_stripTransientCellState()` — re-stripping it here would have reintroduced the artwork-loss regression documented in `debug/CAA-missing-doubled.org`); pure-decoration elements are removed outright; everything else keeps the element and loses only the marker class, because those markers sit on genuine MusicBrainz content (`jesus2099userjs81127recording` is stamped on the recording title anchor itself). An unrecognised future marker defaults to the safe "strip, don't remove" path. The plugin `title` and its yellow `text-shadow` are dropped from marker-carrying `<th>`/`<td>` only — native MusicBrainz puts meaningful `title`s on `<a>`/`<abbr>`, and a `text-shadow` with no jesus2099 marker belongs to an unrelated third-party script (30 such elements in `debug/therising.html` alone), so neither may be stripped blind.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Scope note: the purge is confined to the `table.tbl` elements this script renders. Everything jesus2099 puts outside them — its sidebar/sub-header search links, pending-edit counters and its own toolbar (108-123 such markers per page in the sampled snapshots) — is left completely untouched, so the initial page keeps working exactly as before.
